keyVerseText: And over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagerite. All these were the rulers of the substance which was king David's.
rootMeaning: The root of יָזִיז (Yâzîyz) is connected to the Hebrew root זִיז (zîyz), which carries the idea of movement, abundance, and fullness. Literally, it suggests something that is prominent or set in motion, highlighting a sense of being made noticeable or brought to the forefront. This root meaning enriches the understanding of the name יָזִיז as not merely a personal identifier but as one implying prominence or distinction, fitting for an individual entrusted with responsibility.
usageInScripture: The word יָזִיז appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 27:31, where it is used as a proper name referring to an officer of David. The consistent translation as 'Jaziz' underscores its function as a personal name rather than a common noun. This singular occurrence as a name linked to a Hagarite overseeing the king's flocks indicates a trusted leadership role and highlights the integration of diverse peoples within David's administration.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יָזִיז as meaning 'he makes prominent' or 'one who is set in motion' invites reflection on how God elevates and appoints individuals for His purposes. Even a Hagarite named Jaziz, entrusted with royal responsibility, exemplifies God's sovereign provision of leadership beyond ethnic boundaries. This reminds believers that prominence and authority in God's kingdom are ultimately granted by divine appointment, calling us to faithful stewardship in whatever role we serve. It also points to the inclusivity of God's plan, where faithfulness and service transcend heritage while fulfilling His purposes.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 27:31, 'And over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagerite,' the name יָזִיז highlights the prominence and trust placed in this officer by King David. The verse shows Jaziz as a ruler over valuable resources, emphasizing his responsibility and the significance of his role. The meaning of his name enriches this depiction, suggesting that his position was not incidental but marked by God’s enabling to stand out and lead effectively within the king’s administration.
